children.cond: New lethargy, apnea, feed intolerance, temperature instability, or a sudden rise in direct bilirubin in a stable infant

pill.text: Sepsis until proved otherwise: blood culture (line and peripheral), catheter urine culture, antibiotics now; think NEC. The bilirubin follows the infection
Vitamin K IV now (confirm the dose with pharmacy); recheck INR. Not correcting → liver failure: call a transplant center

children.text: Look at stool color at every diaper change; use a stool color card. An unfed infant passes little stool — look harder, not less.

pill.text: Biliary atresia until proved otherwise: ultrasound now, call pediatric hepatology and surgery today. Persistent pallor or rising direct bilirubin → cholangiogram. Never accept PN as the cause of pale stools

children.cond: Pigmented stools, direct or conjugated ≥ 1.0 mg/dL
Pigmented stools, direct or conjugated below 1.0 mg/dL
children.subtext: Not cholestasis now — recheck direct bilirubin every 1–2 weeks while on PN (lesson 02-08)

children.h: 3 · Does the course fit PN cholestasis?

children.text: Fits: PN for 2 weeks or more before the rise, little enteral feeding, NEC, gut surgery or sepsis, and direct bilirubin levels off or falls as feeds advance.
Same day-1 exclusions as any infant: urine culture, TSH and free T4, newborn screen, CMV PCR, INR.
Abdominal ultrasound with Doppler — tell the sonographer the infant is on PN.

children.cond: Course fits, stools pigmented, ultrasound unremarkable
children.subtext: Working label: PN-associated cholestasis once direct bilirubin is ≥ 2.0 mg/dL after 2 weeks or more of PN (Christensen 2007) — treat (step 4) and keep watching (step 5)

children.cond: Cholestasis before PN or after less than 2 weeks of it, rising on full feeds, or not settling after PN stops

pill.text: Not PN cholestasis — full infant cholestasis workup, atresia first

children.text: Feed the gut: trophic feeds early, advance as tolerated; breast milk preferred. Feeds are the most reliable cure.
Change the lipid: stop pure soybean lipid. Use composite lipid with fish oil, or pure fish-oil lipid 1 g/kg/day (the labeled dose and maximum) — choose with the dietitian and pharmacy.
Do not rely on cutting soybean lipid to 1 g/kg/day — it did not prevent cholestasis in a randomized trial (Levit 2016).
Avoid excess glucose and calories; cycle PN when feasible (limited data).
Line care and early treatment of infection — every sepsis is a new hit.
Review copper and manganese in PN while cholestasis lasts.
UDCA: no definitive trial; only by the enteral route, and urine bile acids first.
Direct bilirubin every 1–2 weeks while on PN; stool color daily (expert opinion).

children.cond: Direct bilirubin falls as feeds reach full volume, stools pigmented

pill.text: Continue feeds; recheck until normal. Keep checking stool color until discharge and beyond — a stool card until a month past the due date (lesson 02-08)

children.cond: Rising despite advancing feeds, still raised after PN stops, pale stools, or an abnormal scan

pill.text: Obstruction until proved otherwise: hepatology today; biopsy and cholangiogram. HIDA non-excretion proves nothing on PN

children.cond: Long PN or short bowel with falling platelets, growing spleen, ascites or GI bleeding

pill.text: IFALD with portal hypertension: refer to an intestinal-failure center now; fish-oil lipid; assess fibrosis — bilirubin alone misleads
